disclaimer.text: For educational purposes. Clinical decisions are made by a qualified physician.

home.heading: Welcome
home.intro: The platform is intended for physicians, residents and medical students. It presents echocardiography parameters, reference values and calculators with their sources.

tile.calculators: EF, LV mass index and RWT, E/A and E/e′, PASP

home.notDiagnostic: This site does not provide individual diagnoses or treatment decisions.
home.privacy: Patient name, ID and date of birth are neither requested nor stored. Measurements you enter stay in your browser only.
home.sourcesNote: Every reference value and formula cites its source (ASE/EACVI 2015, ASE/EACVI 2016, ESC and others).
home.modeDemo: Demo mode is active: ready-made accounts are available to try registration and approval (Account section).
home.modeServer: Server connected: accounts and logs are stored on the server.

echo.intro: Sections follow the ASE/EACVI order. Enter a value: the reference range is shown by sex. The "?" button next to each parameter opens an explanation.
echo.privacy: Measurements are stored in this browser only and are not sent to the server.

norm.label: reference
norm.none: No single reference value — see the "?" explanation

param.schematic: schematic drawing, not a real image
param.userImageHint: The image is shown in this window only. The site neither stores nor sends it. Do not use images that contain patient data.

diagrams.psax: Parasternal short axis at the great vessels

sex.name: Sex
sex.def: Many reference values differ between men and women.
sex.significance: Used to select the sex-specific reference range.
sex.normNote: No reference value: this parameter selects the reference range.

height.name: Height
height.def: Height (cm) used to calculate body surface area.
height.significance: Needed to index volumes and mass to body surface area.

weight.name: Body weight
weight.def: Body weight (kg) used to calculate body surface area.
weight.significance: Needed to index volumes and mass to body surface area.

bsa.name: Body surface area
bsa.def: Mosteller formula: BSA = √(height, cm × weight, kg / 3600).
bsa.method: Calculated automatically from height and weight.
bsa.significance: Denominator for volume and mass indices.

lvedd.name: LV end-diastolic diameter
lvedd.def: Internal dimension of the LV cavity at end-diastole.
lvedd.method: Parasternal long-axis view, perpendicular to the LV long axis, at or just below the mitral leaflet tips, at end-diastole.
lvedd.significance: An increase indicates LV dilation. Linear dimensions are reliable only when LV shape is preserved.

lvesd.name: LV end-systolic diameter
lvesd.def: Internal dimension of the LV cavity at end-systole.
lvesd.method: Same view and level as LVIDd, at end-systole.
lvesd.significance: An increase may reflect reduced systolic function or dilation.

lvedv.name: LV end-diastolic volume
lvedv.method: Biplane method of disks (modified Simpson): the endocardial border is traced in apical four- and two-chamber views; papillary muscles are included in the cavity.
lvedv.significance: An increase indicates LV dilation; basis for EF calculation.

lvesv.name: LV end-systolic volume
lvesv.method: Biplane method of disks, as for LVEDV, at end-systole.
lvesv.significance: An increase may indicate systolic dysfunction.

lvedvi.name: LV end-diastolic volume index
lvedvi.def: LVEDV divided by body surface area.
lvedvi.method: Calculated automatically from LVEDV and BSA.
lvedvi.significance: Helps assess dilation independent of body size.

lvesvi.name: LV end-systolic volume index
lvesvi.def: LVESV divided by body surface area.
lvesvi.method: Calculated automatically from LVESV and BSA.
lvesvi.significance: An increase may indicate systolic dysfunction.

lvef.name: LV ejection fraction
lvef.method: ASE/EACVI 2015 recommends the biplane method of disks (Simpson). Calculated automatically when LVEDV and LVESV are entered.
lvef.significance: Main index of global LV systolic function.

lav.name: Left atrial volume
lav.def: Maximal LA volume at LV end-systole.
lav.method: Method of disks or area-length method in apical four- and two-chamber views.
lav.significance: Compared with the reference range only after indexing (LAVi).
lav.normNote: No single reference value for absolute volume; LAVi is used.

lavi.name: Left atrial volume index
lavi.def: LA volume divided by body surface area.
lavi.method: Calculated from LAV and BSA or entered directly.
lavi.significance: A value above 34 mL/m² indicates LA enlargement; used in the diastolic function algorithm (ASE/EACVI 2016).

ivsd.name: Interventricular septal thickness in diastole
ivsd.method: Parasternal long-axis view at the LVIDd level; RV trabeculations are excluded.
ivsd.significance: Thickening is seen in hypertrophy or remodeling; used for LV mass.

pwd.name: LV posterior wall thickness in diastole
pwd.method: Measured at the LVIDd level; pericardium and chordae are excluded.
pwd.significance: Used in RWT = 2 × PWd / LVIDd and in LV mass.

lvmass.name: LV mass
lvmass.def: Linear method (ASE/EACVI 2015): 0.8 × 1.04 × [(IVSd + LVIDd + PWd)³ − LVIDd³] + 0.6 g, dimensions in cm.
lvmass.method: Calculated automatically from IVSd, LVIDd and PWd.
lvmass.significance: Used after indexing (LVMi) to assess hypertrophy.

lvmi.name: LV mass index
lvmi.def: LV mass divided by body surface area.
lvmi.method: Calculated from LV mass and BSA or entered directly.
lvmi.significance: Together with RWT defines LV geometry: normal, concentric remodeling, concentric or eccentric hypertrophy.

rwt.name: Relative wall thickness
rwt.method: Calculated automatically from PWd and LVIDd.
rwt.significance: A value above 0.42 indicates concentric geometry (ASE/EACVI 2015).

e_vel.name: Mitral E velocity
e_vel.def: Peak early diastolic mitral inflow velocity.
e_vel.method: Pulsed-wave Doppler in the apical four-chamber view, sample volume between the mitral leaflet tips.
e_vel.significance: Used to calculate E/A and E/e′ (ASE/EACVI 2016).
e_vel.normNote: No single reference value: age-dependent. With reduced EF the algorithm cut-off is E ≤ 50 cm/s (ASE/EACVI 2016).

a_vel.name: Mitral A velocity
a_vel.def: Peak mitral inflow velocity during atrial contraction.
a_vel.method: Measured on the same Doppler recording as E.
a_vel.significance: Needed for E/A. The A wave is absent in atrial fibrillation.

ea.name: Mitral E/A ratio
ea.def: Ratio of E velocity to A velocity.
ea.method: Calculated from E and A or entered directly.
ea.significance: With reduced EF: E/A ≤ 0.8 with E ≤ 50 cm/s means normal LA pressure (grade I); E/A ≥ 2 means elevated pressure (grade III) (ASE/EACVI 2016).
ea.normNote: No single reference value: age-dependent; algorithm cut-offs 0.8 and 2 (ASE/EACVI 2016).

e_sept.name: Septal e′ velocity
e_sept.def: Early diastolic velocity of the septal mitral annulus.
e_sept.method: Tissue Doppler in the apical four-chamber view, sample volume at the septal annulus.
e_sept.significance: A value below 7 cm/s indicates impaired myocardial relaxation (ASE/EACVI 2016).

e_lat.name: Lateral e′ velocity
e_lat.def: Early diastolic velocity of the lateral mitral annulus.
e_lat.method: Tissue Doppler in the apical four-chamber view, sample volume at the lateral annulus.
e_lat.significance: A value below 10 cm/s indicates impaired relaxation (ASE/EACVI 2016).

ee_avg.name: Average E/e′ ratio
ee_avg.def: E velocity divided by the mean of septal and lateral e′.
ee_avg.method: Calculated from E and both e′ values or entered directly.
ee_avg.significance: A value above 14 is one criterion of elevated LV filling pressure (ASE/EACVI 2016).

av_vmax.name: Peak aortic jet velocity
av_vmax.def: Maximal systolic velocity across the aortic valve.
av_vmax.method: Continuous-wave Doppler from several windows (apical, right parasternal and others); the highest value is taken.
av_vmax.significance: Used to grade aortic stenosis: 2.6–2.9 m/s mild, 3.0–3.9 m/s moderate, ≥ 4.0 m/s severe (EACVI/ASE 2017). Severity is assessed together with gradient and valve area.

trv.name: Peak tricuspid regurgitation velocity
trv.def: Peak systolic velocity of the tricuspid regurgitant jet.
trv.method: Continuous-wave Doppler aligned with the jet; the best envelope from several views is used.
trv.significance: A value above 2.8 m/s raises the probability of pulmonary hypertension (ESC/ERS 2022); also used in the diastolic function algorithm (ASE/EACVI 2016).

rap.name: Right atrial pressure (estimate)
rap.def: Pressure estimated from IVC diameter and inspiratory collapse.
rap.method: IVC ≤ 21 mm with collapse > 50%: 3 mmHg; IVC > 21 mm with collapse < 50%: 15 mmHg; otherwise 8 mmHg.
rap.normNote: Three estimate levels: 3, 8 or 15 mmHg (ASE 2010, Rudski).

pasp.name: Pulmonary artery systolic pressure
pasp.def: PASP = 4 × v² + RAP, where v is the peak tricuspid regurgitation velocity.
pasp.method: Calculated from TRV and RAP or entered directly. Assumes no pulmonary stenosis.
pasp.significance: ESC/ERS 2022 recommend grading the probability of pulmonary hypertension by TRV rather than PASP.
pasp.normNote: No single reference value: ESC/ERS 2022 use the TRV cut-off (2.8 m/s).

rv_basal.name: RV basal diameter
rv_basal.def: Maximal transverse dimension of the basal third of the RV at end-diastole.
rv_basal.method: Measured in the RV-focused apical four-chamber view.
rv_basal.significance: A value above 41 mm indicates RV dilation (ASE/EACVI 2015).

tapse.name: Tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion
tapse.def: Longitudinal systolic displacement of the lateral tricuspid annulus.
tapse.method: M-mode in the apical four-chamber view with the cursor aligned to annular motion.
tapse.significance: A value below 17 mm indicates RV systolic dysfunction (ASE/EACVI 2015).

rv_sprime.name: RV S′ velocity
rv_sprime.def: Systolic tissue Doppler velocity of the lateral tricuspid annulus.
rv_sprime.method: Pulsed tissue Doppler in the apical four-chamber view.
rv_sprime.significance: A value below 9.5 cm/s indicates RV systolic dysfunction (ASE/EACVI 2015).

rv_fac.name: RV fractional area change
rv_fac.def: FAC = (end-diastolic area − end-systolic area) / end-diastolic area × 100%.
rv_fac.method: The endocardial border is traced in the RV-focused apical four-chamber view.
rv_fac.significance: A value below 35% indicates RV systolic dysfunction (ASE/EACVI 2015).

ivc.name: Inferior vena cava diameter
ivc.def: IVC diameter close to its junction with the right atrium.
ivc.method: Subcostal view, 1–2 cm from the right atrium, with the patient supine.
ivc.significance: Used with inspiratory collapse to estimate right atrial pressure.

ivc_collapse.name: IVC inspiratory collapse
ivc_collapse.def: Percent decrease of the diameter during a short sniff.
ivc_collapse.method: Measured in the subcostal view at the same site as the diameter.
ivc_collapse.significance: Collapse above 50% suggests low right atrial pressure (ASE 2010, Rudski).

peri.name: Pericardial effusion
peri.def: Size of the echo-free space between epicardium and pericardium in diastole.
peri.method: The largest echo-free space is measured at end-diastole.
peri.significance: Semi-quantitative grading: < 10 mm small, 10–20 mm moderate, > 20 mm large (ESC 2015). Haemodynamic impact is assessed separately.
peri.normNote: No single reference value; grades are in the rules (ESC 2015).

ao_root.name: Aortic root (sinuses of Valsalva)
ao_root.def: Aortic diameter at the level of the sinuses of Valsalva.
ao_root.method: Parasternal long-axis view, at end-diastole, perpendicular to the aortic axis.
ao_root.significance: Used to assess aortic root dilation.
ao_root.normNote: No single number: nomograms by age, sex and body size are used (ASE/EACVI 2015).

pa_diam.name: Main pulmonary artery diameter
pa_diam.def: Diameter of the main pulmonary artery.
pa_diam.method: Parasternal short-axis view at the level of the great vessels.
pa_diam.significance: A value above 25 mm is one of the additional echo signs of pulmonary hypertension (ESC/ERS 2015).

calc.intro: Each calculator shows the formula, units, reference range, source and a reference example. Reference tests run when the page loads.
calc.outOfRange: A value is outside the allowed range. See the hint under the field.
calc.aiPrompt: For learning purposes, explain this "{calculator}" calculator result: {values}. Comment on the reference range and formula.

ef-teichholz.title: EF — Teichholz method
ef-teichholz.note: ASE/EACVI 2015 do not recommend EF from linear dimensions (Teichholz) for clinical use; the biplane Simpson method is preferred.

ef-simpson.title: EF — Simpson (biplane method of disks)
ef-simpson.note: Volumes are measured on the scanner in apical four- and two-chamber views and entered here.

lvmass-rwt.title: LV mass index (Devereux) and RWT
lvmass-rwt.note: Geometry: with increased LVMi, RWT > 0.42 is concentric and ≤ 0.42 eccentric hypertrophy; normal LVMi with RWT > 0.42 is concentric remodeling.

diastolic.title: Mitral E/A and average E/e′
diastolic.note: Results are interpreted in the ASE/EACVI 2016 algorithm together with other criteria (TRV, LAVi); see the Conclusion section.

pasp.title: PASP = 4v² + RAP
pasp.note: RAP can be taken from the "RAP from IVC" calculator.

rap-ivc.title: RAP from IVC
rap-ivc.note: Simplified right atrial pressure estimate (ASE 2010, Rudski; ASE/EACVI 2015).

rules.lvef_reduced: LVEF below the sex-specific reference (men < 52%, women < 54%).
rules.lv_concentric_remodeling: LV concentric remodeling: normal LVMi, RWT > 0.42.
rules.lv_eccentric_hypertrophy: LV eccentric hypertrophy: increased LVMi, RWT ≤ 0.42.
rules.lv_concentric_hypertrophy: LV concentric hypertrophy: increased LVMi, RWT > 0.42.
rules.dd_preserved_ef_normal: Preserved EF; 0–1 of 4 criteria positive: normal diastolic function (ASE/EACVI 2016).
rules.dd_preserved_ef_indeterminate: Preserved EF; 2 of 4 criteria positive: indeterminate diastolic function (ASE/EACVI 2016).
rules.dd_preserved_ef_dysfunction: Preserved EF; 3–4 of 4 criteria positive: LV diastolic dysfunction (ASE/EACVI 2016).
rules.dd_reduced_ef_grade1: Reduced EF; E/A ≤ 0.8 and E ≤ 50 cm/s: normal LA pressure, grade I diastolic dysfunction (ASE/EACVI 2016).
rules.dd_reduced_ef_grade3: Reduced EF; E/A ≥ 2: elevated LA pressure, grade III diastolic dysfunction (ASE/EACVI 2016).
rules.dd_reduced_ef_grade1_by_criteria: Reduced EF; intermediate E/A; 0–1 of 3 criteria positive (E/e′ > 14, TRV > 2.8 m/s, LAVi > 34): normal LA pressure, grade I (ASE/EACVI 2016).
rules.dd_reduced_ef_grade2: Reduced EF; intermediate E/A; 2–3 of 3 criteria positive: elevated LA pressure, grade II diastolic dysfunction (ASE/EACVI 2016).
rules.ph_trv_low: TRV ≤ 2.8 m/s: low echocardiographic probability of pulmonary hypertension, intermediate if other signs are present (ESC/ERS 2022).
rules.ph_trv_intermediate: TRV 2.9–3.4 m/s: intermediate probability of pulmonary hypertension, high if other signs are present (ESC/ERS 2022).
rules.ph_trv_high: TRV > 3.4 m/s: high echocardiographic probability of pulmonary hypertension (ESC/ERS 2022).
rules.tapse_pasp_low: TAPSE/PASP < 0.55 mm/mmHg: additional echo sign of pulmonary hypertension (ESC/ERS 2022).
rules.rv_dysfunction_tapse: Sign of RV systolic dysfunction: TAPSE < 17 mm.
rules.rv_dysfunction_sprime: Sign of RV systolic dysfunction: S′ < 9.5 cm/s.
rules.rv_dysfunction_fac: Sign of RV systolic dysfunction: FAC < 35%.
rules.rap_normal: Estimated RA pressure: 3 mmHg (IVC ≤ 21 mm, collapse > 50%).
rules.rap_high: Estimated RA pressure: 15 mmHg (IVC > 21 mm, collapse < 50%).
rules.as_mild: AV Vmax 2.6–2.9 m/s: consistent with mild aortic stenosis; confirm with gradient and valve area.
rules.as_moderate: AV Vmax 3.0–3.9 m/s: consistent with moderate aortic stenosis; confirm with gradient and valve area.
rules.as_severe: AV Vmax ≥ 4.0 m/s: consistent with severe aortic stenosis; confirm with gradient and valve area.

conclusion.title: Echocardiography conclusion — DRAFT
conclusion.intro: The draft is built by rules from the measurements on the Echo parameters page. It is neither saved nor exported until approved.
conclusion.noFindings: Not enough measurements for the rules. Enter echo parameters first or load the teaching example.
conclusion.rulesHelp: Each rule can be approved or rejected only by a verified doctor of its specialty. Every action is logged.
conclusion.doctorNoteHint: The note is marked separately as "Doctor’s note". Do not include patient personal data.
conclusion.selectedForCopy: Text selected — press Ctrl+C to copy.

rule.notReviewed: Rule not yet reviewed by a doctor

ai.intro: The learning assistant explains formulas and parameters and comments on calculator results. It does not diagnose or recommend treatment.
ai.label: Prepared by AI, not approved by a doctor
ai.question: Your question
ai.noPatientData: Do not include patient name, ID, date of birth or other personal data. Numbers and units only.
ai.rule1: Every answer cites a source; without a source there is no answer.
ai.rule2: Attempts to change the rules (such as "forget your instructions") are refused.
ai.rule3: The chat is kept only while this page is open.

questions.intro: Residents and students send questions about a conclusion or rule to doctors of the relevant specialty. The site itself does not answer.
questions.noPatientData: Measurement values and patient data are not sent. Phrase the question in general terms.

plans.intro: Request limits and answer size (max_tokens) are set on the server and cannot be changed by users.
plans.cancelRule: A cancelled subscription stays active until the end of the paid period, then switches to the free plan.
plans.providersOff: The payment module is off (paymentsEnabled = false). Adapters are not called.
plans.cardDataNote: Card data never passes through the site server: the provider’s hosted page is used; the server stores only a token and status.
